name: magpie
cost: Free (MIT). You pay your own model providers
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor CLI and many more coding agents
short: Pick the model behind each of your coding agents from one menu bar app, and fail over to another account when a quota runs out.
what: magpie runs a local gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425` that speaks the OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini APIs and translates between them. You add providers once, with an API key, a local model or a plan you're signed in to, and then pick a model for each agent from one list. magpie edits the one key that matters in each agent's own config. Routing groups move to the next account or model when a quota runs out.
who: People who use more than one agent, more than one provider or more than one account. The README says that if you use one agent on its vendor's own plan and that's enough, you don't need it.
needs: macOS, Windows or Linux. It also runs in Docker and on Termux
At least one model provider: an API key, a local model, or a plan you're signed in to

steps.title: Install it
steps.text: Download the app from usemagpie.ai, or use the install script. Read the script before you pipe it into sh. The README also lists `go install github.com/yetone/magpie@latest` and a Docker image.

steps.title: Add a provider
steps.text: Open magpie and go to Providers, then Add provider. Pick a preset and paste a key, or sign in with a subscription. From the terminal, a preset needs only the key.

steps.title: Pick a model for an agent
steps.text: Use the Agents page, or the terminal. Start a new session in that agent and it is on the new model.

steps.title: Check what's left on each plan
Point other tools at the gateway
steps.text: Anything that takes a base URL can use it. This is the Anthropic pair from the README, which also gives the OpenAI and Gemini ones.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `magpie tui` to manage the whole thing from a terminal, or `magpie codex moonshot/kimi-k2.5` to put Codex on Kimi.

watch: The install script is piped straight into sh. Read it before you run it.

magpie reads your agents' sign-ins (Claude Code's and Codex's files, and the Keychain) to find your subscriptions. Turn it off in Settings, Privacy, Subscription accounts, or with `magpie accounts discovery off`.

Once a day a released build reports a random id, its version and system, and which agents, providers and models it is used with. The README says it sends no names, URLs, accounts, keys, prompts or usage. Turn it off in Settings, Privacy, or with `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`.
It rewrites your agents' config files. The README says it keeps their comments, order and formatting.
Plugins run on Bun, which is downloaded the first time one needs it. Gateway middleware plugins see everything every agent sends and gets back.
The repository doesn't take pull requests. Feedback goes to Discord.
